steps.body: Multiplying resizes a number, and the multiplier tells you which way. When you multiply by a fraction **less than 1** — where the top is smaller than the bottom, like 3/4 — the result shrinks. So 6 × 3/4 is less than 6. You don't have to compute it to know it got smaller.

predict.prompt: 6 × 3/4. Before building anything — will the answer land above 6, below 6, or exactly on it?

options.label: Below 6 — because 3/4 is less than one whole
Above 6 — multiplying always makes things bigger
Exactly 6 — the fraction just rearranges it

predict.reveal: Below. "Multiplying makes things bigger" is only true for factors above 1. Build 3/4 and look at the bar: it is less than one whole, so taking 3/4 OF something can only give you less than you started with.

widget.prompt: Build 3/4 and compare the bar to one whole — that comparison is the whole answer.

commonFractions.feedback: 4/3 is more than one whole — that is the fraction that would make 6 GROW. Swap the numerator and denominator back.
One whole leaves 6 exactly where it was. 3/4 is less than that, which is why the product drops below 6.

widget.lowFeedback: Still short of 3/4 — add more quarters.
widget.highFeedback: Past 3/4 now — take some away. Watch whether the bar stays under one whole as you do.
widget.successFeedback: 3/4 sits below one whole, so 6 × 3/4 must sit below 6 — it is 4.5. The rule is not "multiplying makes it bigger"; it is "multiplying by MORE than one makes it bigger, and by less than one makes it smaller."

hints: Is 3/4 less than, equal to, or more than 1?
explanationVariants: A multiplier under 1 always shrinks the number.
A multiplier above 1 always grows the number.

widget.prompt: Is 8 × 7/6 bigger than 8, smaller than 8, or exactly 8?

options.label: Bigger than 8
options.feedback: Right — 7/6 is more than 1 (7 > 6), so multiplying grows 8.

options.label: Smaller than 8
options.feedback: 7/6 is more than 1, so it grows the number. Smaller would need a multiplier under 1.

options.label: Exactly 8
options.feedback: Only ×1 keeps it the same. 7/6 is more than 1, so 8 × 7/6 is bigger.

steps.body: A fraction that equals 1 — any number over itself, like 4/4 or 3/3 — keeps the value unchanged. 6 × 4/4 = 6. So the whole rule is one comparison: top < bottom shrinks, top > bottom grows, top = bottom stays the same.

explanationVariants: Equal top and bottom means the multiplier is 1.

widget.prompt: A student says 10 × 3/3 = 30. Is the product bigger than 10, smaller than 10, or exactly 10?

options.label: Exactly 10
options.feedback: Right — 3/3 equals 1, so it leaves 10 unchanged.

options.label: Bigger than 10
options.feedback: 3/3 is exactly 1 (top = bottom), so nothing grows. It stays 10.

options.label: Smaller than 10
options.feedback: 3/3 equals 1, so it doesn't shrink either. It stays exactly 10.

widget.prompt: Which multiplier would make a number BIGGER?

options.feedback: Right — 5/4 is more than 1 (5 > 4), so it grows the number.
3/4 is less than 1, so it shrinks. To grow, the top must be bigger than the bottom.
2/5 is less than 1, so it shrinks. A grower has its top bigger than its bottom, like 5/4.

explanationVariants: Only a fraction with top > bottom makes things bigger.
Top under bottom means a shrinking multiplier.

widget.prompt: Without calculating, is 12 × 5/6 bigger than 12, smaller than 12, or exactly 12?

options.label: Smaller than 12
options.feedback: Right — 5/6 is less than 1 (5 < 6), so it shrinks 12.

options.label: Bigger than 12
options.feedback: 5/6 is under 1, so it shrinks, not grows. Bigger needs top > bottom.

options.label: Exactly 12
options.feedback: 5/6 isn't 1 — its top and bottom differ — so the value changes. It's smaller than 12.

explanationVariants: A multiplier above 1 grows 9 to something bigger.

widget.prompt: Without computing: is 9 × 4/3 bigger than 9, smaller than 9, or exactly 9?

options.label: Bigger than 9
options.feedback: Right — 4/3 is more than 1 (4 > 3), so it grows 9.

options.label: Smaller than 9
options.feedback: 4/3 is more than 1, so it grows, not shrinks. Smaller needs a multiplier under 1.

options.label: Exactly 9
options.feedback: 4/3 isn't 1 (top and bottom differ), so the value changes. It's bigger than 9.

takeaways: Multiplying by a fraction under 1 (top < bottom) shrinks the number.
Multiplying by a fraction over 1 (top > bottom) grows it.
A fraction equal to 1 (top = bottom) leaves it unchanged — no computing needed.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Compare the multiplier to 1.** Top smaller than bottom (like 2/3) means less than 1, so the number shrinks. Top bigger than bottom (like 5/3) means more than 1, so it grows. So 10 × 2/3 is less than 10 — no computing needed.

explanationVariants: Top under bottom means a shrinking multiplier.

widget.prompt: Is 10 × 2/3 bigger than 10, smaller than 10, or exactly 10?

options.label: Smaller than 10
options.feedback: Right — 2/3 is less than 1 (2 < 3), so it shrinks 10.

options.label: Bigger than 10
options.feedback: 2/3 is under 1, so it shrinks. Bigger needs top > bottom.

options.label: Exactly 10
options.feedback: 2/3 isn't 1, so the value changes — it's smaller than 10.
